passage: In the Singapore office, Xin was promoted after presenting the vendor-cost analysis that Wei had mostly built. Wei clapped with everyone else, and his jaw ached. For days he replayed the meetings in his head and felt bitter. Then, at Friday's team review, he noticed that nobody but him knew which parts were his. He had emailed the files to Xin and never written a word about them. That afternoon Wei sent a short note to the team lead listing what he had built and asked to present the next analysis himself. Xin, passing his desk, gave a small nod, and Wei could not tell whether it meant sorry or good luck.

qa.q: What was Wei feeling while he clapped for Xin?
qa.a: Wei felt bitter; his jaw ached and he kept replaying the meetings, even though he clapped.

qa.q: What did Wei do that was more useful than resenting?
qa.a: Wei wrote to the team lead listing what he had built and asked to present the next analysis himself.

qa.q: How might Xin have seen the situation?
qa.a: Xin may have thought sharing files was ordinary teamwork, and the small nod suggests Xin noticed Wei's point, though its meaning stays unclear.

grounding: A colleague feels bitter when the credit-taker is promoted, then makes his own work visible instead of resenting.

The branch staff room was loud with cake and congratulations. Rukmini had been made team lead, mostly on the strength of the loan-tracking sheet that Tanvir had built and she had presented.

Tanvir took a small piece of cake and ate it standing near the window. When Mrs D'Souza from operations asked him why he was quiet, he said, "Nothing. Good for her." His jaw was tight.

That evening he kept rereading the announcement email. He noticed that his name wasn't in it anywhere, but also that he had never once written his manager about the sheet himself.

The next Monday Tanvir sent a short weekly update to the branch manager: what he built, what it saved, what came next. At the Friday review he asked for five minutes to demo the new version himself.

Watching Rukmini clap for his demo, he felt a strange mix of envy and relief. The bitterness hadn't gone, but it was getting quieter.

qa.q: Who had built the loan-tracking sheet?
qa.a: Tanvir had built the loan-tracking sheet.

qa.q: What does Tanvir's tight jaw while saying "Good for her" suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Tanvir felt bitter and envious about Rukmini's promotion, even while trying to sound pleased.

qa.q: What changes did Tanvir make, and why do they help?
qa.a: He began sending weekly updates to the branch manager and presented his own work at the review, making his contribution visible instead of only resenting.

qa.q: How might Rukmini feel watching Tanvir's demo?
qa.a: Rukmini might feel awkward or a little exposed, but also relieved that Tanvir is getting credit openly, since she clapped for the demo.

grounding: Shows a young worker envious that a credit-taking colleague was promoted, who learns to make own work visible instead of resenting.

passage:
Subject: long rant, sorry

Hi Anjali,

Siddharth got promoted today. Senior analyst. Most of the client model he presented in March was my work, and he said "I built" at least four times.

I smiled at the team lunch. Then I sat in the washroom for ten minutes because I didn't trust my face. I've been bitter all week, checking his profile, counting his compliments. It's exhausting.

But here's the uncomfortable part. I never told anyone what I did. I just assumed people would notice. They didn't.

So I'm trying something. From Monday I'll send my lead a short Friday note: what I did, what's next. I've also asked to present my own section at the quarterly review. Scary.

I'm not okay with what Siddharth did. I'm just done letting it eat my evenings.

Call this weekend?
Deepika

qa.q: When had Siddharth presented the client model?
qa.a: Siddharth presented the client model in March.

qa.q: How was Deepika feeling during the week, and what shows it?
qa.a: Deepika felt bitter and envious; Deepika hid in the washroom after lunch and kept checking Siddharth's profile and counting his compliments.

qa.q: What small step is Deepika taking, and why is it a good one?
qa.a: Deepika will send a short Friday note to the lead and present at the quarterly review, making the work visible rather than waiting to be noticed.

qa.q: If you were Anjali reading this email, what might you want to say?
qa.a: Anjali might want to say that the anger is fair and the plan sounds brave, and offer to talk it through on the weekend call.

grounding: Shows a young employee bitter that a credit-taking colleague was promoted, choosing to make own work visible instead of resenting.
